A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Camber study. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover all 47 and 48 pages, including Appendices A–E, without material reading gaps. Expanded bibliography entries account for the additional page.

before.justification: v2 reports original privacy-judgment experiments on PrivacyLens+ and ConfAIde+, expansion comparisons, and human-annotation analyses in Sections 4–6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original model experiments, human-judgment analyses, and supplementary results in Sections 4–6 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Camber's label-independent, label-dependent, and reasoning-guided expansion procedures are identical in Section 5 and Appendices C–D, including code identification and context generation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same information-sharing appropriateness tasks using PrivacyLens+, ConfAIde+, and their context expansions. No datasets, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same no-expansion, label-independent, and label-dependent comparisons, evaluated with Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-4.1, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet. Bibliographic revisions do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Model versions, sample sizes, generation procedures, prompt variants, metrics, and temperature/output settings remain identical in Sections 4–6 and Appendices B–E.

E4.justification: Prompt-sensitivity tests, code-generalization analyses, human/model entropy comparisons, and qualitative expansion-error studies are unchanged in Section 6 and Appendices A–B.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 95% bootstrap confidence intervals using 1,000 resamples, three expansion runs in Figure S3, and the same repeated model judgments and human annotations used for entropy analysis.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match across the main text and appendices. For example, Table S5 reports the same 95.3% F1 for Gemini 2.5 Pro's consent-based expansion on PrivacyLens+.

T1.justification: The scenario formalization, performance-metric definitions, and non-adversarial assumption in Section 3 are unchanged. No mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about context ambiguity, reasoning-guided disambiguation, accuracy improvements, and reduced prompt sensitivity.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are identical, including qualifications about synthetic clarifications, real-world applicability, code generalization, and the reliability of individual model rationales.

D1.justification: Reference [3] removes the ConfAIde benchmark repository URL and MIT License note. The authors' dataset link, implementation details, compute disclosures, and full generation/evaluation prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 34 cited works and research positioning are retained. Changes to entries such as MuSR, GoldCoin, and Ghalebikesabi et al.'s form-filling work concern author, title, and publication metadata rather than added research or revised relationships.

P1.justification: Editing is confined to bibliography wording and metadata, capitalization, and the arXiv version/date stamp. Main-text and appendix prose, terminology, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Longer bibliography entries change line wrapping and redistribute references across three pages instead of two. All figures, tables, captions, and appendix page bodies remain visually identical after matching pagination.

improvement.justification: Fuller bibliographic details modestly improve reference documentation, while removing ConfAIde's source URL and license note reduces access documentation. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, limitations, and methodological appendices are identical, and the authors' dataset link remains. These limited changes leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
